The NB states a free action of the unit group (underlined Z/h underlined Z) with handwritten superscript star, commuting with W. It asserts that two cyclic lines are in the same orbit of that group exactly when they have the same stabilizer in W.

math_checks.check: Consequence of commuting actions for stabilizers
math_checks.work: For a in the acting unit group and w in W, commutation gives w(aD)=a(wD). Since a is invertible, w(aD)=aD if and only if wD=D. Thus Stab_W(aD)=Stab_W(D).
math_checks.result: This verifies the same-orbit implies same-stabilizer direction directly from the commuting-action hypothesis printed here. Freeness is not needed for this implication.
math_checks.limits: The converse, existence of the action, and its freeness are asserted on the page and were not proved.

math_checks.work: For a finite transitive W-action on these lines, the map W to the orbit of D has fibers the cosets of Stab_W(D), so the number of lines is card(W)/card(Stab_W(D)). Substituting the displayed cyclic stabilizer and, conditionally, its order h gives card(W)/h.
math_checks.result: The written denominator h is consistent with a cyclic stabilizer of order h.
math_checks.limits: This is an elementary conditional count. I did not establish the order of a Coxeter element from this page, nor prove the claimed transitivity or the primitive-eigenvalue uniqueness assertion.
